nodes.description: mapping(address => uint256) private _balances in HedwigInu; stores token balances and is mutated by _transfer.
mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) private _allowances; spender approvals, written by _approve and read by allowance.
uint256 private _tTotal = 1000 * 10**9 * 10**18; fixed total supply read by totalSupply().
address private _owner in Ownable; written in the Ownable constructor and renounceOwnership, read by owner().
address private newComer = _msgSender(); used by the onlyOwner modifier instead of _owner, an inconsistent/backdoored ownership check.
msg.sender, the caller-controlled address returned by _msgSender() and used for balances, approvals and ownership checks.
constructor of HedwigInu: assigns the entire _tTotal to _msgSender() and emits Transfer.
name() public view returns the _name string constant.
symbol() public view returns the _symbol string constant.
decimals() public view returns _decimals (18).
allowance(address owner, address spender) public view returns _allowances[owner][spender].
approve(address spender, uint256 amount) public; forwards to _approve with _msgSender() as owner.
transferFrom(address sender, address recipient, uint256 amount) public; calls _transfer then decrements the allowance via SafeMath.sub.
totalSupply() public view returns _tTotal.
balanceOf(address account) public view returns _balances[account].
transfer(address recipient, uint256 amount) public; forwards to _transfer from _msgSender().
_approve(address from, address to, uint256 amount) private; privileged branch when from == owner(), otherwise silently sets allowance to 0 and emits Approval(from,to,4).
_transfer(address sender, address recipient, uint256 amount) internal; moves balances using SafeMath add/sub and emits Transfer.
owner() public view in Ownable returns the _owner state variable.
renounceOwnership() public onlyOwner; sets _owner to address(0).
transferOwnership(address newOwner) private onlyOwner; unreachable externally, updates _owner.
onlyOwner modifier that compares msg.sender to newComer (not _owner), giving an incorrect authorization gate.
_msgSender() internal view from Context, returns msg.sender; the single trusted-input gateway of the contract.
Address.sendValue performs recipient.call{value: amount}("") after a balance check; external value transfer that can invoke an attacker contract.
Address._functionCallWithValue performs target.call{value: weiValue}(data) on an arbitrary target with unbounded calldata.
Balance arithmetic in _transfer: _balances[sender].sub(amount) and _balances[recipient].add(amount) (SafeMath-wrapped, arithmetic risk category).

edges.reason: _msgSender() returns the untrusted msg.sender, making it the input gateway for all caller identity.
Constructor mints the whole supply to _msgSender(), i.e. the deployer address.
approve() uses _msgSender() as the allowance owner.
transferFrom() uses _msgSender() as the spender whose allowance is decremented.
transfer() uses _msgSender() as the sender of the transfer.
onlyOwner compares _msgSender() with newComer, so caller identity directly drives the authorization decision.
The Ownable constructor stores _msgSender() in the local variable msgSender.
Local msgSender is assigned into the _owner state variable during construction.
Constructor writes the full total supply into _balances for the deployer.
Constructor reads msg.sender to determine the initial balance holder.
spender argument flows into approve() and then into the allowances mapping.
amount argument flows into approve() and then into the allowances mapping.
owner argument indexes the _allowances mapping in allowance().
spender argument indexes the _allowances mapping in allowance().
account argument is used to look up _balances in balanceOf().
recipient argument flows into transfer() and onward to _transfer().
amount argument flows into transfer() and onward to _transfer().
sender argument of transferFrom() is passed to _transfer() and used as allowance owner.
recipient argument of transferFrom() is passed to _transfer().
amount argument of transferFrom() is used both in _transfer() and in the allowance subtraction.
from argument indexes _allowances and is compared against owner() in _approve().
to argument is the approved spender key written into _allowances.
amount argument is the value written into _allowances (or zeroed in the non-owner branch).
sender argument indexes _balances for the SafeMath subtraction inside _transfer().
recipient argument indexes _balances for the SafeMath addition inside _transfer().
amount argument drives both balance arithmetic operations in _transfer().
newOwner argument is written into _owner by transferOwnership, guarded by onlyOwner.
approve() delegates all allowance logic to the private _approve().
transferFrom() calls _transfer() to move the tokens.
transferFrom() calls _approve() afterwards to decrement the caller's allowance.
transfer() calls the internal _transfer() helper.
_approve() writes the _allowances mapping, either the requested amount for the owner or 0 for everyone else.
_transfer() reads and writes the _balances mapping for sender and recipient.
_transfer() performs the balance subtraction/addition that constitutes the arithmetic sensitive operation.
Result of the SafeMath balance arithmetic is written back into _balances.
balanceOf() reads the _balances mapping.
allowance() reads the _allowances mapping.
totalSupply() returns the _tTotal state variable.
owner() returns the _owner state variable.
renounceOwnership() overwrites _owner with address(0) under the onlyOwner gate.
transferOwnership() overwrites _owner with the new address under the onlyOwner gate.
onlyOwner reads the newComer state variable instead of _owner, so ownership checks are bound to a different storage slot.
The onlyOwner modifier gates execution of renounceOwnership().
The onlyOwner modifier gates execution of transferOwnership().
_approve() calls owner() to decide between the privileged and the zeroing allowance branch.
Address.sendValue performs an unbounded value call to a recipient contract, which can re-enter state-mutating functions such as _transfer before bookkeeping finishes.
Address._functionCallWithValue forwards an arbitrary low-level call to a target contract, allowing re-entrant invocation of token transfer logic.
